about: The ground right round the City in 1986-1988, for a sense of scale: the streets, the dirt paths, the courts and the fences. src/surroundings/ground.js paints the features on the ground. Plan frame: x right, z down the plan, metres. Sources: survey sheet 11-NE-11A (May 1987) and the 1989 Lambot aerial (Wikipedia's lead photo of the City), fitted to the plan frame (error about 2-4 m by the City, more far out). The park paths are on the 1989 photo, not on the 1987 sheet: they were built in 1987-89. The NW court is on the 1987 sheet and gone by 1989. Each feature has its source.

features.name: Tung Tau Tsuen Road, carriageway (north)
features.source: SOURCED: kerb lines read on survey sheet 11-NE-11A (May 1987) in the plan frame, x -125..80
features.why: The street on the north face. It is about 14 m kerb to kerb (13.3-14.7 m). context.json has two centre lines here (road:9024, 9.3 m; road:12782, 10.6 m). Together they paint about 17-19 m, and road:9024 runs 1-3 m onto the City side of the south kerb.

features.name: Tung Tau Tsuen Road, south footway (City side)
features.source: SOURCED: the kerb, from 11-NE-11A (May 1987). INFERRED: the inner edge is the City face of data/plan.json, set 0.5 m clear
features.why: A strip of 1-5 m between the kerb and the City buildings. The sheet draws no other line here. That it was a footway is INFERRED.

features.name: Tung Tau Tsuen Road, north footway (Mei Tung side)
features.source: SOURCED: the north kerb and the Mei Tung Estate boundary line, from 11-NE-11A (May 1987)
features.why: About 6-8 m between the north kerb and the estate boundary.

features.name: Tung Tsing Road, carriageway (east)
features.source: SOURCED: kerb lines read on 11-NE-11A (May 1987), z -40..125
features.why: About 5-6 m kerb to kerb along the east face (z -40..70), with a 2-3 m footway on its east side. South of the side-road junction at z 75-88 it widens to 10-12 m. The context centre line road:9016 lies 2-4 m east of the 1987 kerbs at z -35..30.

features.name: Lung Chun Road strip along the south face
features.source: SOURCED: the name LUNG CHUN ROAD and the lot fence, from 11-NE-11A (May 1987). SOURCED: the width and the dirt, from the 1989 Lambot aerial (camera fit, see notes). The inner edge follows the City face of data/plan.json, with the notch at x -13..-7
features.why: From the SW corner to x 24, the 1989 photo shows a strip of dirt, low shrubs and debris 4-6 m wide. It lies between the south face and the paved park promenade. East of x 24, it runs 8-12 m wide between the face and the court fence, with a line of trees on the 1989 photo. The sheet draws no south kerb: the road was open to the cleared ground.

features.name: Dirt strip along the west face
features.source: SOURCED: 1989 Lambot aerial (camera fit, see notes). The widths are measured from the foot of the facades, and set out from the City face of data/plan.json
features.why: A dirt strip 7.5-14 m wide along the whole west face, NW corner to SW corner. Its outer edge is the edge of the 1988-89 park path. It is 12-14 m wide at z -50..-5 and z 35..62, and 7.5 m wide by the two pavilions at z 4..25. A pale low wall or kerb runs about 2-3 m out from the facades (INFERRED from the photo).

features.name: Footpath FP from Tung Tau Tsuen Road south (NW)
features.source: SOURCED: "FP" on 11-NE-11A (May 1987). The surface is INFERRED
features.why: About 3 m wide, between a solid line and a dashed line. It leads south from the road to the NW basketball court.

features.name: Footpath FP west of the NW court
features.source: SOURCED: "FP" on 11-NE-11A (May 1987). The surface is INFERRED
features.why: About 4-5 m wide, between the solid line at z -45.5 and the dash-dot fence of the court.

features.name: Basketball court enclosure (NW)
features.source: SOURCED: "Basketball Court" and its fences on 11-NE-11A (May 1987). The west end lies under the sheet-edge lines: x -150 is INFERRED
features.why: About 22 x 17 m. It is gone by 1989: the photo shows park rockeries there.
features.courtsSource: INFERRED: the sheet draws no markings; one court along the long side of the fenced ground.

features.name: Basketball court ground (south of the east half)
features.source: SOURCED: the "Basketball Courts" outline on 11-NE-11A (May 1987). The 1989 aerial shows the same paved ground
features.why: 74 x 33-37 m, turned about 3.5 deg. In 1989 three courts are marked on it (see courts). context.json covers only its part at z > 95.6.
features.courtsSource: SOURCED: the ground, from 11-NE-11A (May 1987). SOURCED: the markings, from the 1989 Lambot aerial rectified to the plan frame: key/three-point arcs at both ends, centre line z 100.7, sidelines x 56, 69.5, 73, 87.5, 91.5, 104.5, post bases at the north ends. Each court 26 x 14 m (the old FIBA size): INFERRED from the line spacing.

features.name: Football field
features.source: SOURCED: the dashed fence "Football Field" on 11-NE-11A (May 1987); a tall fence on the 1989 aerial
features.why: About 48 x 66 m, turned about 3 deg. It lies at z 126-195, outside the plate. context.json openGround "Football field and basketball courts" already covers it.

features.name: Fence: south lot line and court fence round to Tung Tsing Road
features.source: SOURCED: dashed fence with ticks on 11-NE-11A (May 1987)
features.why: East of x 40 the fence stands 2-3 m off the south face. It turns south along the west side of Tung Tsing Road.

features.name: Fence: north side of the court ground
features.source: SOURCED: line with ticks on 11-NE-11A (May 1987); a row of trees along it on the 1989 aerial
features.why: Ticks with small triangles. It can be a low retaining wall (INFERRED).

features.name: Fence: south lot line west of x 40
features.source: SOURCED: dashed line with ticks on 11-NE-11A (May 1987)
features.why: 1-2 m out from the face. LUNG CHUN ROAD is lettered just south of it at x -38..-5.

features.name: Cleared ground west and south of the City (inside the plate)
features.source: SOURCED: 11-NE-11A (May 1987) draws nothing here but "CIP June 1986" and "Construction in Progress May 1987". context.json openGround "Sai Tau Tsuen ground (cleared)" covers the same ground outside the plate
features.why: The ground of the cleared squatter village (Sai Tau Tsuen). It was a building site for the park in 1986-88. By 1989 it is the park, with paved paths (see the two park paths). Paint it under the strips, the courts and the paths.

features.name: Park path along the west face (1988-89, not on the May 1987 sheet)
features.source: SOURCED: 1989 Lambot aerial (camera fit; absolute error about 3-6 m)
features.why: Grey, crisp-edged, 6-8 m wide. It was built with the park after May 1987. Leave it out for 1986-87. On the photo it sets the outer edge of the west dirt strip.

features.name: Park promenade along the south face (1988-89, not on the May 1987 sheet)
features.why: A grey band 8-9 m wide (z about 76-85), 4-6 m south of the face. The photo shows people on it. Its tone and kerbs match the curving park paths, thus it is paved (INFERRED). It was built after May 1987.
